audit_notes: Parameters positive and within bounds. Streamwise permeability of parallel slots K_x = phi s^2/12 = 0.75*9e-10/12 = 5.63e-11 m2 (sqrt 7.5 um); spanwise/wall-normal permeability 2.25e-12 m2 (sqrt 1.5 um). Net slip length b = (sqrt(K_x) - sqrt(K_z))/alpha = 6.0 um; b/H = 0.24; laminar Couette wall-shear reduction b/(H+b) = 19.4 % at fixed sublayer-edge velocity. This is an upper bound: the virtual-origin theory gives Delta U+ ~ l_x+ - l_z+ = 1.25 in wall units (delta_nu = 4.8 um), i.e. ~6 % turbulent skin-friction reduction at Cf = 1.5e-3, and DNS of anisotropic permeable walls show the benefit collapses once sqrt(K_y+) exceeds ~0.4 (here 0.31, margin small: at 10 m/s delta_nu drops to ~3.9 um and sqrt(K_y+) = 0.38). Validity conditions: substrate depth must exceed ~3 sqrt(K_x) ~ 25 um so the Brinkman layer is fully developed; the perforated lid must keep wall-normal permeability as low as the spanwise one. Structural: lamellae ~10 um thick, a few tens of um tall in a hard polymer under 50 Pa shear and ~150 Pa pressure fluctuations: no collapse; hydrostatic pressure acts on both sides of the water-filled lattice, so no crushing. Main non-physics risk: biofouling inside the lattice (5 um lid holes admit bacteria and diatoms), which would clog canals and remove the anisotropy; this does not make the concept infeasible but needs a fouling-release material and is documented as the key risk. Baseline: impermeable smooth wall (slot_width = 0 and spanwise_permeability = 0 give zero slip).
